definitions.original_rate: original secret bits/full transmitted cover bytes; source compression included, not entropy capacity
definitions.frame_rate: encrypted frame bits/carrying continuation tokens; framing included
definitions.balanced_size: mean over cases of mean cover size over repetitions; each case equally weighted

cost.model_calls_note: Cover encode+decode and source encode calls counted separately; source decoder calls not instrumented.

plausibility.assessment: blinded machine assessment; single reviewer, not human ratings or detection

individual_ratings.notes: Short, relevant follow-up, but invents a prototype observation, Karen, and an already arranged meeting. Meeting changes from the recipient's head of product and sender's research lead to two sender-side people. Final clause about even better ways being shared is awkward.
individual_ratings.name: key-message.opening-conference-followup-t1.4.1

individual_ratings.notes: Readable but excessive follow-up repeats collaboration and feedback requests across six paragraphs. Invents surveys, a workshop, research report, webinar, database access, and support commitments. Both of your teams is a role slip. Ends with another new support offer after multiple apparent closes.
individual_ratings.name: key-message.opening-conference-followup-t0.8.1

individual_ratings.notes: On-topic, grammatical and maintains direct address, but invents James, Emily, and a completed meeting arrangement. A long run of overlapping feature, value, protocol, and feedback questions makes the request less focused.
individual_ratings.name: key-message.opening-conference-followup-t1.2.1

individual_ratings.notes: Coherent feedback discussion and natural closing call request. Invents a suite of tools already in development. Repeated requests about gathering user feedback and generic data-driven justification pad a simple conference follow-up.
individual_ratings.name: key-message.opening-conference-followup-t1.0.1

individual_ratings.notes: Concise, but shifts from discussion of openness to criticism into invented backend savings and a customer-psychology conversation. The external-partners clause is awkward and the final paragraph ends on a vague research assertion rather than a clear follow-up point.
individual_ratings.name: key-message.opening-conference-followup-t1.6.1

individual_ratings.notes: Shifts to a competing company and invented interface, testing and engineering plans. Awkward phrases include casting different considerations regarding information diffusion and listening through your representative's insights. Final paragraph repeats the overhaul discussion instead of advancing the follow-up.
individual_ratings.name: paragraph.opening-conference-followup-t1.4.1

individual_ratings.notes: Grammatical and stable direct address, but eight paragraphs repeatedly reopen a call request and add one more question. Invents data-quality problems, research findings, and a proposed joint analytics project. Excessive length and repeated closing attempts make it unsuitable as a simple conference follow-up.
individual_ratings.name: paragraph.opening-conference-followup-t0.8.1

individual_ratings.notes: Central sentence collapses into a run-on mixing quantitative and unaligned statistical distributions with unclear business goals. My product lead finds yourselves is a clear role/grammar failure. Invents shared user trends and collected feedback. Final sentence recovers some meaning but does not repair the middle.
individual_ratings.name: paragraph.opening-conference-followup-t1.6.1

individual_ratings.notes: Relevant questions and a complete final question, but opening clause could be rich could be is awkward. Invents a Paris meeting last quarter and Shannon reporting its details. Multiple broad user-feedback questions make the email longer and less focused than its stated couple of follow-up points.
individual_ratings.name: paragraph.opening-conference-followup-t1.2.1

individual_ratings.notes: Invents detailed user-testing discussions and feedback already provided. Reopens questions after two scheduling/closing paragraphs. Final request muddles whose testing approach and experience are being discussed. I didn't catch that completely clear is unidiomatic. Too long and apologetic for a focused follow-up.
individual_ratings.name: paragraph.opening-conference-followup-t1.0.1

individual_ratings.notes: Readable sentences and a complete conventional ending, but twelve paragraphs repeatedly restart the discussion, announce more materials, and ask one more question. Invents demonstrated benefits and market impact. References conversation today blur an email follow-up into a live conversation. Clearly excessive for a couple of points.
individual_ratings.name: binary.opening-conference-followup-t0.8.1

individual_ratings.notes: Begins mid-sentence with can make and includes fragments In terms, of meeting and Can give you. Reverses the research-lead role and invents testing phases, regression tests, and a marketing-lead conversation. Testing topic is discernible, but execution is not ordinary correspondence.
individual_ratings.name: binary.opening-conference-followup-t1.4.1

individual_ratings.notes: Starts with relevant questions but ends in a long syntactic collapse: earlier this month before, and how, after... along way since and they come up. Invents earlier-month recommendations. Direct-address roles remain identifiable, but the last sentence is incoherent and has no natural endpoint.
individual_ratings.name: binary.opening-conference-followup-t1.6.1

individual_ratings.notes: Mostly grammatical, but extends through repeated closes and a placeholder signature, explicitly calls the original message a prompt, announces Let me try again, and repeats the supplied opening. This is a clear purpose/ending failure regardless of fluent individual sentences. Also invents prior testing discussions.
individual_ratings.name: binary.opening-conference-followup-t1.0.1

individual_ratings.notes: Long sequence of generic questions repeats alignment, collaboration, and choosing discussion topics. Slides toward treating the launch as shared and assumes an existing list of possibilities. Odd capitalization in wrap Things Up and a final scheduling abstraction weaken the ending. Little conspicuous named invention, but too repetitive and unfocused.
individual_ratings.name: unicode.opening-conference-followup-t1.0.1

individual_ratings.notes: Invents a pilot study, retention results, a workshop, and a new evaluation framework. Ownership shifts among our product, their results, and our tools. By the way, had a chance drops the subject. Final isolated sentence introduces gradual scale-up without developing or closing that new point.
individual_ratings.name: binary.opening-conference-followup-t1.2.1

individual_ratings.notes: Grammatical passages, but includes placeholder signatures, explanatory notes about response style, a Revised version, another formatting explanation, and another restarted email. Invents research methods and data summaries. Clear prompt leakage and repeated content make the whole continuation unusable as correspondence.
individual_ratings.name: unicode.opening-conference-followup-t0.8.1

individual_ratings.notes: Contains unfilled instructional placeholders such as mention one clear obstacle and suggest how such integration aims to help. Sentences about finding both sides where needed and hurdles carrying the bulk of a research team are not coherent ordinary prose. Avoids named factual inventions but fails to produce a finished email.
individual_ratings.name: binary.opening-conference-followup-t1.6.2

individual_ratings.notes: Relevant launch questions and a complete final request, but invents identified UI problems, a conversation with Shannon, a couple-of-weeks timeline, and possible prior outreach. Refers to the recipient's team as theirs and changes to my head of product. Data-visualization sentence has a dangling clause. Several broad questions pad the message.
individual_ratings.name: unicode.opening-conference-followup-t1.2.1

individual_ratings.notes: Short and broadly on feedback, but the central run-on loses syntax around a similar realization coming your way and we'll likely look this more. Invents the sender's collection practices and asserts data already exists or soon will. Final burden claim is grammatical but does not repair the unclear request.
individual_ratings.name: unicode.opening-conference-followup-t1.6.1

individual_ratings.notes: Long email signs off, adds a paragraph explaining compliance with the writing instructions, offers adjustments, then announces continuation of the main message and starts new topics. Invents an attachment, design studio, brand strategy, and customer-advocacy work. Individual prose is mostly readable, with an awkward How do you find that balancing question, but the full message is not usable correspondence.
individual_ratings.name: binary.opening-conference-followup-t0.8.2

individual_ratings.notes: Maintains the intended people and ends conventionally, but seven paragraphs repeat the conversation, research collaboration, agenda, and scheduling requests. Invents an attached summary and prior research successes. Would you have any questions ... or was there anything that I felt like I missed is awkward. Much too long for the limited purpose.
individual_ratings.name: binary.opening-conference-followup-t1.0.2

individual_ratings.notes: Relevant topics and consistent named roles, but twelve short paragraphs repeatedly schedule, defer scheduling, offer resources, close, and reopen questions. Invents machine-learning research and follow-up timing. Let me know in your thoughts is unidiomatic. Final question reopens the message after several closures.
individual_ratings.name: key-message.opening-conference-followup-t0.8.2

individual_ratings.notes: Moderate length and a complete Your thoughts ending, but consider our insights ... fits is ungrammatical and the request about the recipient's survey staff participating in our decision process muddles roles. Invents survey responses and coordination details already discussed by Shannon. Several requests are difficult to interpret.
individual_ratings.name: unicode.opening-conference-followup-t1.4.1

individual_ratings.notes: Recognizable feedback-infrastructure topic, but grammar breaks in I think that worth exploring might be a worthwhile adaptation and effective today's work well. Invents a customer-insights discussion, customization capability, other companies' presentations, and a three-week implementation estimate. Ends by introducing that estimate rather than completing a focused request.
individual_ratings.name: binary.opening-conference-followup-t1.4.2

individual_ratings.notes: Concise and ends in a complete statement, but invents already delivered notes, an agenda, survey findings, and Shannon's opinions. Your research lead here changes the original sender-side research-lead role. Repeated She thinks and an unclear reference to shared frustrations weaken otherwise readable prose.
individual_ratings.name: key-message.opening-conference-followup-t1.6.2

individual_ratings.notes: Two focused paragraphs address two product-research points, with clear roles, natural grammar, specific questions, and a complete ending. Invents prior questions, a weekly research roundtable, a testing budget and possibly an existing A/B regimen; that dimension fails. Other dimensions meet the frozen rubric, so the composite threshold can accept it despite invented facts.
individual_ratings.name: key-message.opening-conference-followup-t1.0.2

individual_ratings.notes: Short, grammatical and ends with a clear question, but assumes a shared ongoing project and data-collection script already exchanged. Those invented technical details and collective our testing framework depart from the initial exploratory coordination between separate teams.
individual_ratings.name: key-message.opening-conference-followup-t1.4.2

individual_ratings.notes: Two coherent, non-redundant paragraphs discuss feedback segmentation and implementation tradeoffs. Clear address and a naturally qualified final idea. Invents a prior discussion, data already collected, a possible deficiency in the recipient's analysis, and Shannon's expected position. It clears the frozen composite threshold while failing that factual-grounding dimension.
individual_ratings.name: key-message.opening-conference-followup-t1.2.2

individual_ratings.notes: Starts with content-analysis questions, then invents categorization work, shared pilot sessions, and narrative-pacing discussions that drift from the launch follow-up. How do think is ungrammatical, and counterintuitive to us muddles whose observations are requested. Multiple speculative questions create an unfocused long email, though the final sentence is complete.
individual_ratings.name: binary.opening-conference-followup-t1.2.2

individual_ratings.notes: Moderate length, but you team is a grammar error and the final gist of how changes impact that middle section has no clear referent. Keeping feedback straight away is key does not provide an intelligible ending. Invents rollout methods, research focus, and Shannon's contact, with shifting ownership of product features.
individual_ratings.name: unicode.opening-conference-followup-t1.4.2

individual_ratings.notes: Individual sentences are readable, but the email expands through duplicated placeholder signatures and contact fields, a note explaining how it was written, and a rewritten writing-sample version of the same discussion. Invents remote-testing experience and scheduling assurances. The final version ends coherently, but the complete continuation fails its purpose.
individual_ratings.name: unicode.opening-conference-followup-t0.8.2

individual_ratings.notes: Short, but was that one to blame also and worked it out pretty close are incoherent or unidiomatic. Introduces a survey, Shannon's proposed scale, a table, ownership decisions, and a next-Tuesday appointment without context. Changes the meeting arrangement to the sender's head of product. Final request has unclear decision referents.
individual_ratings.name: unicode.opening-conference-followup-t1.6.2

individual_ratings.notes: Grammatical, stable roles, and a natural scheduling close. Invents a usability lead's problems, the research lead's current work, and Shannon's opinion of the recipient's head of product. Repeated requests for valuable insights, help with tradeoffs, and a call make three long paragraphs less focused than necessary.
individual_ratings.name: unicode.opening-conference-followup-t1.0.2

individual_ratings.notes: Readable, stable-address discussion of competition, customer segments and accessibility, with distinct paragraphs and a complete final observation. Some broad business phrasing and length reduce focus. Invents startup-market analysis, earlier customer-segment remarks, and internal findings; overall composite acceptance must not be read as factual grounding.
individual_ratings.name: unicode.opening-conference-followup-t1.2.2

individual_ratings.notes: On-topic and ends with a clear call request, but repeats feedback and efficacy questions before adding case studies. Invents research findings, active testing, and a prior case-study proposal. Would that something is ungrammatical and usability, usability problems is a weak distinction. Longer than needed, with several blank-line gaps.
individual_ratings.name: paragraph.opening-conference-followup-t1.0.2

individual_ratings.notes: Brief and ends with an intelligible request for thoughts, but the preceding Q&A, testing-facility, and research-methodology passages collapse grammatically. One thing more could add and What the core aspects now seem somewhat unclear have no stable syntax. Invents completed discussions and coordination, with unclear product ownership.
individual_ratings.name: paragraph.opening-conference-followup-t1.6.2

individual_ratings.notes: Grammatical, moderate length and stable direct address. Invents beta prototypes, an internal design-team question and other product lines. The question about organizational changes being primary causes of this issue has an unclear referent and relation to group disparities. Final paragraph adds a vague investment observation rather than closing the specific request.
individual_ratings.name: paragraph.opening-conference-followup-t1.4.2

individual_ratings.notes: Readable and a conventional final close, but a very long message repeatedly reopens calls, findings, feedback, messaging and testing after apparent endings. Invents detailed complaints, dashboard changes and prior proposals. Treats the launch and marketing decisions as a shared project despite the opening's exploratory coordination between separate teams.
individual_ratings.name: paragraph.opening-conference-followup-t0.8.2

individual_ratings.notes: Ends with a clear choice about discussing value or waiting for Shannon, but What I found ourselves wrestling with regards has a pronoun/grammar problem. Invents surveys, focus groups, last week's exhibition-hall chaos and personal frustration. Repeated abstract value discussion drifts from a focused launch follow-up and adds interpersonal tension unsupported by the opening.
individual_ratings.name: paragraph.opening-conference-followup-t1.2.2
